pages.text: Whales and Dolphins

image.note: Cover: a great blue whale with a dolphin alongside

pages.text: Contents. Giants of the Sea / Not Fish at All / How They Live / Talking in the Deep / The Biggest of All / Sharing the Ocean.

Somewhere in the ocean, at this very moment, swims the largest animal that has ever lived on earth, larger than any dinosaur, with a heart the size of a small car. It is a whale. And near it, perhaps, a pod of dolphins races and leaps, clever and playful and full of chatter. This is the story of the giants and geniuses of the sea.

image.note: A vast whale and leaping dolphins in the ocean

pages.text: Whales and dolphins live their whole lives in the water, and it is easy to think they are simply very large fish. But they are not fish at all. They are something far more surprising, and once you know what they truly are, you will never look at them the same way again.

image.note: A whale and a dolphin swimming together

pages.text: Whales and dolphins belong to the same great family, and dolphins are really just small, quick whales. They come in many sizes, from dolphins no longer than you, to whales longer than three buses in a row. All of them are beautifully built for a life in the water: smooth, sleek, and powerful.

image.note: A size line-up: dolphin to giant whale

pages.text: They glide through the sea with a few strokes of their great tails, which beat up and down, not side to side like a fish. Some can dive deeper than a mountain is tall, into the cold and darkness, and hold their breath for an hour or more before rising again for air.

image.note: A whale diving deep with powerful tail strokes

pages.text: Here is the great surprise. Whales and dolphins are not fish. They are mammals, warm-blooded animals, just like you, and dogs, and lions. They do not lay eggs, but give birth to live young, and feed their babies on milk, just as your mother once fed you.

image.note: A mother whale with her calf, feeding it

pages.text: And, like you, they cannot breathe underwater. A fish can take air from the water through its gills, but a whale cannot. It must come up to the surface to breathe, through a blowhole on the top of its head, breathing out in a great misty spout, then holding its breath and diving down again.

image.note: A whale breathing out a misty spout at the surface

pages.text: Long, long ago, the ancestors of whales did not live in the sea at all. They walked on land, on four legs. Over millions of years, they returned to the water, and slowly changed, their legs becoming flippers and tail, until they became the ocean giants we know. Whales are, in a way, animals who went back to the sea.

image.note: An ancient four-legged whale ancestor beside a modern whale

pages.text: Whales and dolphins are hungry animals, and they eat in different ways. The great whales have no teeth for chewing. Instead, their mouths are lined with giant bristly combs, and they gulp huge mouthfuls of sea water full of tiny creatures, then push the water out and swallow the food left behind.

image.note: A great whale feeding through its bristly comb

pages.text: Dolphins and the smaller whales do have teeth, sharp and many, and they hunt fish and squid, chasing them down with speed and cleverness. Often they hunt together, a whole pod working as a team, herding the fish into a tight ball where none can escape.

image.note: A pod of dolphins herding fish together

pages.text: Whales and dolphins are among the cleverest animals on earth, and they are great talkers. They fill the sea with sound: clicks, whistles, squeaks, and, most wonderful of all, the long, haunting songs of the great whales, which travel for miles through the water.

image.note: Sound travelling through the sea between whales

pages.text: Dolphins use sound to see, as well as to speak. They send out clicks, and listen for the echoes bouncing back, and from those echoes they can tell exactly what lies ahead, even in the dark or muddy water. It is a kind of hearing that paints a picture, and it is astonishingly good.

image.note: A dolphin sending clicks, echoes returning as a picture

pages.text: They live in close family groups, and care for one another. They play, they help the sick and the young, and they seem to know each other as friends. Some scientists believe dolphins even call each other by special whistles, like names. There is a great deal of cleverness swimming in the sea.

image.note: A close family group of dolphins together

pages.text: And now, the greatest of them all: the blue whale, the largest animal that has ever existed, in all the long history of life on earth. It is longer than three buses, and heavier than thirty elephants. Its heart alone is the size of a small car, and a child could crawl through its largest blood vessels.

image.note: The colossal blue whale, with a bus for scale

pages.text: And yet this giant of giants eats some of the smallest creatures in the sea: tiny shrimp-like animals, no bigger than your fingernail, which it swallows by the tonne. The biggest animal that ever lived is fed by some of the smallest. There are few stranger, grander facts in all of nature.

image.note: The huge blue whale feeding on tiny creatures

pages.text: For a long time, people hunted whales in great numbers, and many kinds became rare. Today, most of the world protects them, and their numbers are slowly climbing again. But the ocean they live in needs our care too, kept clean and full of life, for the giants and the geniuses depend upon it.

image.note: Whales swimming in a protected, healthy ocean

pages.text: So somewhere out in the wide blue sea, right now, a great whale is singing, and a pod of dolphins is racing the waves, and the largest heart on earth is beating, slow and strong, in the largest animal that ever lived. The ocean holds wonders, and these are among its very greatest.

image.note: Whales and dolphins thriving in the open sea

pages.text: Words to know. Mammal: a warm-blooded animal that feeds its young on milk. Blowhole: the nostril on a whale's head for breathing. Pod: a family group of whales or dolphins. Blue whale: the largest animal that has ever lived. Echo: a sound bouncing back, used by dolphins to see.

image.note: Labelled diagram of a whale and a dolphin

pages.text: The ocean is full of astonishing life, from the giant whale to the tiny shrimp it eats. And the land and sky have their own wonders. Which creatures of our living world will you meet next?

image.note: The rich variety of ocean life
